key_insight: Non-Gaussian input states can unlock positive quantum capacity for the bosonic thermal attenuator in noise regimes where all single-mode Gaussian states fail.
engineering_relevance: This expands the design space for bosonic quantum communication systems by showing that carefully chosen non-Gaussian encodings can preserve quantum information at higher thermal noise.
method: Proved the best single-mode Gaussian coherent-information lower bound equals the classic thermal-state bound.
Constructed an explicit rank-two non-Gaussian state supported on six Fock levels with positive coherent information.
Numerically optimized fixed non-Gaussian families to obtain stronger certified rates near the thermal threshold.
evidence_signal: At environment thermal photon number ν=1, the authors certify positive coherent information down to transmissivity η=0.7841, including 4.7×10^-4 qubits/use from an explicit witness and up to 8.4×10^-3 qubits/use numerically.
watch_item: The certified non-Gaussian witness is far from numerically optimal, so practical encoding/decoding performance may require more complex state preparation and control.
paper_title: Bosonic quantum communication beyond the thermal threshold
